values: SWRL rules over observations detect abnormal situations; C-SPARQL stream reasoning over observations; alignment of SOSA to DUL.
SHACL rules compute derived values and aggregates over observations with automatic unit conversion; features are platform parts linked by hasPart.
Neural networks and CEP rules are described as s3n:Algorithm procedures with ssn:hasInput/ssn:hasOutput subclasses and memory requirements as ssn-system conditions, inside WoT Thing Descriptions.
Observations subclassed per domain (EarthquakeObservation, AQObservation); SHACL shapes validate SOSA data, e.g. one sensor per observation collection.
A virtual sensor implements a detection query; events and states derived from observations with causal knowledge between state types and topological relations through hosting.
Mobile sensors whose observations are coordinates (m2ssn:MobileSensor); complex event detection over multimedia sensor observations.
AI models are sosa:Procedure instances with ssn:hasInput/ssn:hasOutput and REST endpoints; controllers typed with invented terms in the sosa namespace (sosa:MachineAutomation, sosa:MachineSetting).
Observations subclassed per quantity (TempValue, HumidityValue, CO2level); sensors linked to observations by own per-quantity properties (:hasSmokeValue); SWRL rules over results raise fire risk.
Virtual sensors and actuators (vhbieo:VirtualSensor) for immersive virtual environments next to in-situ ssn:Sensor; survey answers treated alongside observations as data of an occupant.
Observations subclassed per feature type (RoadObservation, IncidentObservation, ActivityObservation); a shortcut property from road to length besides the observation.
Observations subclassed per meaning and rule outcome (ExhibitProximityObservation, ObservationToHighLevelEnergy) with SWRL rules deciding lamp brightness.
Observation IRIs minted from the OPC UA nodeId and the timestamp; RML stream mapping from OPC UA.
hasSimpleResult mapped as subproperty of domain quantity properties (Length, Volume); SWRL rules over observations infer hazards.
Observations are observedBy the weather station; observation IRIs encode timestamp, station and property; a quality value per observation.
Gateways and LoRa nodes modelled as platforms for connectivity management; hardware vs software sensors.
Cameras are the features of interest of aggregated count observations, the aggregation tool being the sensor; aggregation function given by cot:usingFunction.
Inspections as sosa:Procedure (eurotl:InspectionActivity) used by condition observations; an agent takes the sensor role.
Observations as time-annotated named graphs in RDF streams consumed by real-time agents; misspelled sosa:simpleResult.
Observations and results subclassed per quantity (TemperatureObservation, TemperatureResult); qudt:QuantityValue and geo:Geometry declared subclasses of sosa:Result; stored in Neo4j.
A Part-Observation-Property design pattern; farm operations with input and output products via ssn:hasInput/ssn:hasOutput.
Observations kept as rows of a time-series database with sosa:madeBySensor, quantity, unit, value and timestamp columns, federated with Brick/BOT graphs.

Sensors and algorithms point to OBOE characteristics (orka:observesCharacteristic) rather than sosa:observes; a SWRL rule makes the hosting robot the feature of interest of proprioceptor observations.
ssn:System given an ethics mode (:hasEthicMode) and privacy attributes from ColPri; SEAS connections between systems.
Aggregators typed dashb:AggregatedObservableProperty; units and data types on a separate metric node; sensor annotations on a Web Thing gateway drive dashboards.
Metadata nodes attached to observations (mmo:hasMetadata, mmo:Frequency); a SWRL rule infers ssn:isProxyFor from a stimulus; SOSA terms written in the ssn namespace.
Measurement and Instrument subclass sosa:Observation and sosa:Sensor; diagnoses as prov:Activity over measurements; designed for relational databases.
Reuses a non-existent sosa:ObservationValue; actuations are HTTP requests with OWL-S preconditions and effects for AI planning.
dcat:Dataset declared a subclass of sosa:Result to point to files and external databases (dcat:DataService) from observations.
Signals (time series kept outside the graph) are attached to hosted devices by properties such as ev:ActivePower and queried with a SPARQL extension instead of observations.
IRIs built from relational primary keys of the WoSIS database; SPARQL queries over SOSA graphs used to generate a SensorThings API.
Actuator modules linked to agricultural properties by ssn:forProperty; observations named by kind (NDVIObservation) as individuals.
Signal classes carry OWL restrictions on their sensor and unit; sensors and actuators are classes linked by sosa:isObservedBy/isActedBy restrictions.
Shortcut roles (speed, pos, acceleration) defined by role chains hosts • madeObservation • hasResult from a platform to measured values.
Mapping of the FIESTA-IoT ontology (old SSN) to OMA NGSI context entities.
Quality-of-context indicators (precision, freshness) attached to observation results.
Provenance (prov:wasGeneratedBy) held at the observation-collection level; flow paths between subsystems by downstreamOf.
The measurement capability of the sensor is linked to the feature of interest of the observation.
Measurements hang off asset states (AssetState → Measurement) with an uncertainty value; measurement IRIs embed probe and timestamp.

SensorThings API entities mapped to SOSA with OWL functional and inverse-functional constraints to detect inconsistencies; result and unit arrays of MultiDatastreams lose their pairing when flattened.
ssn:observedProperty given on raster scientific field layers (ex:BaseLayer with rows, cols, WKT bbox) rather than on observations.
Alignment only: weather station deployment details aligned with ssn:Deployment, co-iot entities with ssn:Platform; m3-lite quantity kinds reused.
Time granularity terms invented in the ssn namespace (ssn:Day, ssn:Hour).
Security metadata (access control, authentication provider) attached to IoT-Stream streams generated by SOSA sensors.
A processing step loosely linked to sosa:Observation and sosa:Sample, Procedure being judged broader.
Ground motion represented as sampled time steps with a quantity kind and a direction (NS, EW, V).
Observable properties modelled as a DUL:Role that an object property plays given the sensing capabilities, not as an intrinsic quality.
SOSA classes referenced from OpenAPI schemas by an x-refersTo annotation (a smart door as sosa:Actuator).
Planning agents aligned with sosa:Platform, with location and time on agent states.
A hosts property relates a welding machine to the part it welds; whether it is sosa:hosts is not shown.
The work's ContextAttribute class is declared equivalent to sosa:Observation.
System capabilities (operating power range, response time, measurement range) describe the sensors.
